subject: Delete _shared_modules/engineer_features.py after per-notebook migration
description:
DECISION (Brian, 2026-08-12): no shared feature-engineering module. Danskvand has zero promotional measures (confirmed on the fresh extract, F23), so a single shared path is untenable. Each category notebook adapts its own feature engineering from the CSD gold standard.

NOT DONE YET -- deleting now would break four pipelines. Verified live importers:
  Danskvand: pre_danskvand_4_engineer_features.py:42, _5_apply_split.py:37, _6_save_outputs.py:41
  Energidrikke: pre_energidrikke_4:42, _5:37, _6:41
  RTD: pre_rtd_4:42, _5:37, _6:41
  CSD notebook: imports filter_series, engineer_features, apply_split, build_series_index
                (the notebook does NOT inline this logic -- P0030 made keeping it an import a hard constraint)

Per Brian sequencing: "The CSD specific feature engineering is the current gold standard for CSD and needs to be adapted to the other datasets based on their structure. We will do this once CSD is done." Deletion is the LAST step of that migration, not the first.

ORDER:
1. Finish CSD (P0036 tasks 4, 6) -- CSD notebook is the reference implementation.
2. Inline the four imported functions into the CSD notebook (make_calendar, filter_series, engineer_features, apply_split, build_series_index). Preserve the V3 promo_intensity lag fix and the ffill-only make_calendar fix (F16) -- made ONCE in the shared module, must survive into every copy.
3. Build per-category notebooks from the CSD template, adapting for capability tier (F23):
     CSD 32 cols / 7 promo | Energidrikke 32 / 7 (2 renamed) | RTD 31 / 6 (NO sales_units_any_promo, so promo_units not derivable as in CSD) | Danskvand 15 / 0 promo
4. Retire the per-category pre_*_N_*.py step scripts they replace.
5. THEN delete _shared_modules/engineer_features.py and update all references.

KEEP: terminal_utils.py, timing_utils.py, base_preprocessing.py -- print/timing/boilerplate helpers, not feature logic.

RISK: duplicating logic 4x is exactly the drift P0027/P0029/P0030 fought. The V3 and bfill fixes each needed making only once BECAUSE the module was shared. After the split, any future leakage fix must be applied 4 times. Record in Ch10; consider a shared TEST suite running the same leakage assertions against all four notebooks outputs.

Verify: no live .py or .ipynb imports engineer_features; all four categories run end-to-end; leakage assertions pass for each.
